The autumnal dawn’s light seeped through his curtains that bright morning, gentle breeze and browning leaves signposting the end of the dry summer, which means it perfect harvesting season for Phainon and his family. His phone lit up in a frenzy of light, blaring that stupid fucking Living Tombstone FNAF song he set as his alarm back when he was what, twelve? His phone kept hammering out the electrical cords at full blast until Cyrene nearly destroyed his door by smashing it in at 6:30 AM on a Monday morning, indicating the start of the academic year of Phainon’s shitty senior year.

What the fuck is going on?

He squinted his eyes, despite not adjusting to the light that shone on his mathlete and chess tournament trophies that glittered in his room like stars, mounted behind them were shining framed posters of his favourite video games, flanked by numerous figurines from anime franchises along with comic book characters in a multitude of poses that he bought from numerous conventions in the past with his money he made off of those nationwide tournaments he won, like the fucking nerd he is.

He haphazardly searches for his glasses, considering he is nearly half blind without them (and annoyingly, his ‘friends’ joke about how he is still blind with them on due to the interesting fashion choices he has made in the past), then gets changed into a safe combination of a red, washed out, well-loved t-shirt that barely covered his broad frame and a pair of loose black jeans, alongside some light styling of his hair (please read: he brushed it). After brushing his teeth and checking if he needs to replace his power chains or not, he stumbles down the stairs with his rucksack dangling off his shoulder, littered with badges, keychains and pins he’s collected over the years. 

“Hey, you fucking bum, wake up on your first alarm. I can’t stand hearing that fucking song or whatever every morning because you’re too lazy to turn it off.” Cyrene calls out from the kitchen, currently constructing a sandwich for Phainon’s lunch.

“Also- huh? Did you get bigger? What are you preparing for? Warfare? Y’know Weird Uncle Lygus would recruit you at the next family gathering- he thinks you’re overdeveloped and he’s right.” Cyrene poked his arm and gestured at his burly physique. “The only thing he complains about is your lack of abs and how you’re fat. Ignore him, he’ll get arrested before anything happens because of his ankle monitor.”

Sorry what? Why is she saying I’ll get drafted by Uncle Lygus? He’s always on some substance and chanting about killing god, so I’ll ignore him since no one likes Lygus. Also-

“Do you mean the Living Tombstone? And no, I won’t wake up just because it bothers you. You know, I’ll deliberately sleep through it just to piss you off.”

Phainon not so elegantly swipes the sandwich off the counter, and books it out of there before she’s about to obliterate him.

Phainon tramped through the front gates and into the bright, gleaming hallways and almost wishes to disintegrate right then and there because of tacky nature of the school’s decorations that are way too polished for 8 AM on a Monday. Thankfully, entertainment that comes in a human form greets him almost immediately.

“Hey loser!” 

Phainon turns his head to meet Cipher gazing back at him with that look in her eye that screams trouble.

“Oh, hey Cipher! Didn’t see you there. How was your summer?” Phainon innocently answered back, knowing the dangers of Cipher’s activities.

“As awkward as ever, Snowy. I’ve, y’know, just been scamming people, vandalising and terrorising the locals as per usual.” She grinned, showing off her new (and probably d.i.y) piercings she donned, one of many that littered her face nowadays. It suited her though.

“But I know damn well you did jackshit over summer, so I’m not asking you how that was.”

Damn it. She didn’t have to point that out.

 

“Yeah well, I was- I was doing something! I went to ComicCon! That’s something!” He tried to rebuttal, which to Phainon’s luck, never worked.

“Okay dipshit I don’t care about that.”

Cipher’s verbal torrent kept bombarding him as he shrank further into himself in the middle of the corridor, glasses slipping down his nose as he nervously bit into his lip. 

“Awww, little Snowy went outside once during his whole six-week break! Let’s give him an applause!” She said in a mocking tone of faux fondness, slowly clapping, as resonated down the hallway like an echo booming at the start of a lowly boss fight in one of the shitty indie games, he played at 2:15 AM instead of sleeping.

“Yeah- okay well fuck you Cipher. I’m leaving.”

“Yeah, fuck you too, you little cunt.”

Phainon sauntered into his first class of day, already wishing he could kill himself. 

After a few hours of torture from his philosophy class with Professor Anaxa…gora? Gorus? He’s not entirely sure, he sits down amongst the infamous trio of troublemakers and pulls out his sandwich - which he checks to confirm its his favourite pickle and peanut butter sandwich - as Stelle, Dan Heng, and March start arguing about who the best character was next to him, and it started getting pretty heated after about 10 seconds. Phainon looked around, surveying the area trying to search for his two friends that he knew were skiving their practise in some classroom.

“Hey guys, have you seen Cipher and Hyacine?” Phainon asks them as he slowly turns to face them, only to be met with Stelle diving on top of March because she liked someone else other than Cerces.

“Oh, I believe they went to get lunch before cheerleading practice. They may come through here in a bit to get to the fields to train.” Dan Heng helpfully supplied as he ignored to calamity occurring in front of him, for his own peace of mind. 

And low and behold, when you speak of the devil she will appear.

“Hey nerds! What’s up?” Cipher approaches the table with Hyacine in tow and-

“Hey. My name’s Mydeimos, you can call me Mydei.”

This breaks Phainon out of his out of body experience. 

“Oh- um hi Mydei! It’s nice to meet you! Are you off to cheerleading p-practice too?” Phainon inquired while nervously smiling, flashing his braces he just gotten tightened the previous week. 

In the background, Cipher muttered bitterly, “Oh so he answers him and not me. Got it.”

“Yeah, I’m on my way to training now. It was nice meeting you…” Mydei trailed off, unsure of his name.

“Oh I’m- “

“That nervous wreck is called Phainon. He’s a loser. Don’t talk to him.” Cipher butted in.

Here, have this to wipe your face down.” Mydei digs around in his bag, only to pull out an embroidered pink handkerchief that had his name decorated with flowers on it, rimmed with lace. “Hey, Phainon?”

He turned around, only to be met with a girl he’s seen before in his science class. Phainon tried to remember her name, but he couldn’t for the life of him, and to be honest, he didn’t really care. If she was anything like Mydei he would have not even forgotten hername to begin with.

She answered him, “I was wondering if you were free this afternoon, I need some help with our recent topic… and um… I think you’re the best at explaining things…” She trailed off as she investigated the distance over his shoulder. 

“Well, this is rather short notice. I’m sorry but I’m busy later. Maybe some other time?” Phainon responded but was met with silence from his classmate. 

He noticed she was looking over his shoulder, frozen with her eyes glazed over, his answer going completely over her head as she nervously backed away from him. 

“Y-yeah… maybe another time. I’ll see you later.” She sped off down the hallways in the opposite direction of Phainon, desperate to escape the suffocating presence consuming the hall behind Phainon. 

He turned around, only to be met with nothing. What was her deal?

You know how ear-grating it is to even listen to you speak, let alone with your braces taking it up a few thousand notches.” Cipher grumbled out, rather unhappy with the fact someone swiped the last chocolate milk carton from under her nose before she got a chance to pick it up a few moments prior, causing her to take her frustration on Phainon, the conventional human target.
